text:
The classic triad of postpartum fever, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling lochia (implied by the clinical context of endometritis) strongly points to an infection of the uterine lining. Given the risk factors of prolonged labor and large infant, and the absence of urinary symptoms, endometritis is the most likely diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometritis
